data.content_ref: inline:SCR_001's suppression ratio S/(S+E) is structurally incompatible with the neighbourhood's counter-conditions because it is a population-level frequency metric, whereas every counter-condition (universal grammar, non-cross-cutting problems, spanning sets) is a per-problem structural property. A lineage can have a high suppression ratio yet zero genuine suppression if its problems are intrinsically non-cross-cutting (SRC_002's counter-condition), inflating S with false positives. The metric contradicts the foundation's causal requirements unless the denominator includes a structural-eligibility filter. It is refuted if there exists no problem class where L_rival produces a valid non-native solution but the problem is still provably non-cross-cutting under SRC_002's definition, which would mean S is always a clean signal.
